transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because the doctor doing my insurance physical recently told me my weight was too low. I guess they wanted me to get it checked out. 

Honestly, I don't really see it. To me, I just look lean. I'm a painter, so I'm always up and down on ladders and working really long days. It just makes sense that I'd be on the leaner side, but... yeah, that's why they sent me in.
How do you feel about the idea of gaining weight — does that thought worry or concern you at all?

Yeah, I guess it does bother me. If the scale goes up even a little bit—like after a dinner with a client or if I eat something with bread—I actually get pretty tense about it. When that happens, I usually start cutting back on what I eat the next day just to make sure the extra weight doesn't stick. So, yeah, the thought of gaining weight definitely worries me.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, how do you see your body—do you feel you look too thin, about right, or actually overweight in some areas?

I definitely don't see myself as too thin. Honestly, when I catch myself in a mirror, or... like, if I see photos of myself standing next to one of my murals, I'm mostly just checking specific spots. I basically judge my whole day by whether my stomach and my face look sharp enough. 

If they look a little soft or round, it really bothers me. So I guess I'd say I feel like I need to keep those areas in check, rather than ever thinking I look underweight.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, or if you know it, your most recent BMI?

I honestly don't remember the exact numbers from that physical. The doctor might have told me my BMI, but I didn't really commit it to memory. 

As for my weight, I mean, I weigh myself at home, but it fluctuates a little depending on the day... so I'm not exactly sure what my official weight is right now. I just know they said the number was too low.
Besides cutting back on food, have you ever done anything else to control your weight—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising specifically to burn off what you ate?

No, I haven't done any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives, and I don't really exercise either. I mean, my job keeps me pretty active, being up on ladders and moving around all day painting, but I don't work out on purpose to burn calories. If I feel like I've had too much, I just eat less the next day. That's pretty much it.
Do you know your current height, so we can work out an approximate BMI together?

I'm actually not totally sure. I haven't been measured in a really long time, so... I don't want to give you the wrong number. I'm just sort of average height, I guess, but I don't know the exact feet and inches right now.
Compared to a year or two ago, have you noticed any noticeable weight loss, like clothes fitting looser or needing a smaller size?

Not really, no. I mean, I mostly just wear the same work clothes... the same pants I've had for a couple of years now. They fit about the same, I guess. I haven't had to go out and buy a smaller size or anything like that.
Have you noticed any physical changes lately, like feeling unusually cold, more tired than usual, dizzy, or any hair thinning or loss?

No, I haven't really noticed any of that. I feel fine, honestly. I'm not unusually cold or dizzy or anything like that. And my hair is... well, it's just normal. I get tired after a long day on the job, sure, but just the regular amount, you know? Nothing out of the ordinary.
Would you be willing to be weighed and measured here today so we can get an accurate current height and weight?
Honestly, I'd... I'd really rather not do that today. I don't really see the need for it, since like I said, I feel perfectly fine. I'd prefer to just skip the scale, if that's alright with you.
Even if you don't remember exact numbers, do you recall whether the doctor at your physical described your weight as only slightly below normal, or significantly underweight for your height?

He just said it was too low. That's actually the whole reason I came in—the doctor doing my insurance physical flagged it and told me I needed to be seen. I don't remember if he used the word 'significantly' or not, just that my weight was too low for my height. 

I mean, I don't really see it. To me, I just look lean from being up on ladders and working long days painting.
Would you be able to get a copy of the results from your recent insurance physical—specifically the weight, height, or BMI they recorded—so we can review the exact numbers together?

I mean, yeah, I guess I could do that. I don't have the paperwork on me or anything right now, but... I suppose I could call the clinic that did the physical and ask them to send the records over. If you really need to see the exact numbers, I can figure out how to get a copy for you.
How long have you been restricting your food intake and feeling this level of concern about your weight and shape—days, months, or longer?

It's been... probably the last year or so, I guess. Though I don't really look at it as restricting. It's just my routine now. Most days I just keep it to coffee, maybe a protein bar between paint jobs, and then a small dinner at night. Eating a full meal just feels like it would slow me down while I'm working, so I just stick to what keeps me moving.
Do you recall roughly what you weighed a year or so ago, before you started cutting back on food, so we can compare it to what you might weigh now?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I didn't weigh myself much back then either. I just know my clothes fit a little looser now, but I couldn't give you an exact number from a year ago.
You mentioned your clothes fit a bit looser—have you noticed needing to move your belt in a notch or two, or any other concrete sign that you've lost a noticeable amount of weight over the past year?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I wear a tool belt a lot for work, and I have had to tighten that up a notch or two over the last few months so it doesn't slide down my hips. And my regular jeans are definitely baggier in the legs and waist. But I don't really track it beyond just noticing things like that.
Even though you're not certain of the exact number, can you give me your best estimate of what your home scale showed the last time you weighed yourself?
I really don't know. I don't own a scale at home. Like I said, I don't really track it, so I haven't weighed myself in a long time.

I mean, I don't really see it. To me, I just look lean from being up on ladders and working long days painting.

Fear of weight gain and body-checking behaviors persist, but actual weight status remains unconfirmed, so AN subtypes and unspecified feeding/eating disorder remain viable.

Eating a full meal just feels like it would slow me down while I'm working, so I just stick to what keeps me moving.

And my regular jeans are definitely baggier in the legs and waist. But I don't really track it beyond just noticing things like that.

Absence of purging, laxative use, or compulsive exercise argues against binge-purge subtypes. Ruled out F50.9 (unspecified) since the pattern now fits fairly typical anorexia nervosa criteria, though confirmation of exact BMI/degree of low weight is still needed to distinguish F50.0 (meeting full weight threshold) from F50.1 (atypical, if weight not significantly low).
